topic: A teacher receives an unexpected gift from a former student
text: The doorbell echoed through the quiet house, a sudden puncture in the silent afternoon. I wasn’t expecting anyone, yet there it was again, more insistent. I made my way to the door, wondering who might be there at this hour. Opening it, I found no one, but on the stoop sat a small, neatly wrapped box. It felt like a question, wrapped in burgundy paper, tied with a thin, silver string. Inside, an old, leather-bound book, its pages yellowed with time. A note slipped out, my name scrawled on it in a familiar but long-forgotten hand. “For the stories you never told,” it read. I ran my fingers over the title, a rush of memories flooding back, of afternoons spent in that classroom, the sun slanting through the windows, and the way words could make the world seem both vast and intimately close.
